topics.label: Introduction to cancer causation and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, lecturer, and core learning outcomes concerning cancer etiology, environmental exposures, and carcinogenicity testing.

topics.label: Genetic and biological drivers of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by a combination of endogenous cellular processes, external mutagens, and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental exposures and epidemiological patterns of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine environmental risk factors, the debate over bad luck versus exposure, and epidemiological evidence demonstrating geographic variations in cancer rates.

topics.label: Infectious agents and the pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how microbial pathogens contribute to cancer, illustrating the concept through the detailed epidemiological and molecular mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific chemical mutagens, metabolic activation pathways, and physical radiation induce structural DNA damage and adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction between tumor initiators and promoters, focusing on the roles of chronic inflammation, signaling mimicry, and developmental life stages in tumor progression.

topics.label: Experimental and epidemiological methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic mutational signatures, population biobanks, animal models, and in vitro assays used to identify and evaluate carcinogenic agents.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by synthesizing the role of environmental factors in cancer and the practical risk-benefit decisions surrounding carcinogen exposure.
